original_question: Which chromosome contains the gene most commonly associated with hereditary hemochromatosis in people of Celtic descent?

final_qi.question: Which chromosome contains the gene most commonly associated with hereditary hemochromatosis in people of Celtic descent?
final_qi.long_answer: The form of hereditary hemochromatosis that predominates in individuals of Celtic ancestry is linked to mutations in the HFE gene (most notably C282Y and H63D). The HFE gene is located on the short arm of chromosome 6 at band 6p21.3, within the major histocompatibility complex (MHC) region. Therefore, chromosome 6 contains the gene most commonly associated with this hereditary iron-overload disorder.
